Service-first shop, not a box-mover — lead with respect for his service reputation
Sells Kaishan compressors — every compressor sale is a treatment attach he's leaving on the table

intel_nuggets: No dedicated dryer/filtration line — drop-ships whatever's cheap when a compressor sale needs treatment. Thin margin, no relationship, no control over lead time.
Sells & services Kaishan rotary screws — the ECOTROC/ECOCLEAN line pairs naturally as a treatment attach on every compressor package.
Was burned by a manufacturer before (backorders blew up a big install) — lead times and support are a scar. Answer it directly.
Two locations, ~18 employees, 3 trucks, ~$6M revenue. Owner-operator — he makes the call, no committee.
Territory is central Indiana into Ohio — the exact Midwest corridor KSI is building out. Lead-feed + co-marketing is a live promise, not fluff.
rapport.opening_line: Hey Dave, I work with independent distributors on the air-treatment side — I had a question about how you handle dryers and filtration on your Kaishan compressor sales.
rapport.adapted_script: This is a DISTRIBUTOR recruitment call — talk to him like a distributor, never an end-user. Lead with the gap: he sells Kaishan compressors but has no dryer/filtration line, so he drop-ships treatment at almost zero margin. Frame KSI as (1) real margin on a line he OWNS, (2) German engineering that protects his service reputation, (3) qualified lead-feed + co-marketing in his central-Indiana-into-Ohio corridor, (4) responsive support and honest lead times — this directly answers his backorder scar, (5) a treatment attach on every compressor he already sells. Products: ECOTROC KTA-S refrigerated dryers, ECOTROC DDAP desiccant, ECOCLEAN APF filtration. Avoid: sounding scripted, corporate fluff, or pitching him like he's buying one dryer.
watch_outs: He built this up himself — respect his independence, don't be pushy
Been burned on backorders — lead time and support are the objection under every other objection. Answer it head-on.
Talk distributor economics (margin vs drop-ship), not end-user features — treating him like a buyer of one unit loses him
SCOPE: KSI's line here is dryers and filtration ONLY — keep the recommendation to those
product_reference: ECOTROC KTA-S — refrigerated dryers, 14 to ~1,890 CFM, ~$1,880 up to ~$47,000. The everyday attach on a Kaishan compressor sale — real margin on a line he owns vs. a drop-shipped catalog dryer.
ECOTROC DDAP — desiccant dryers for low-dewpoint / critical air. Higher ticket, higher margin, the answer when a refrigerated dryer isn't enough.
ECOCLEAN APF — coalescing + particulate filtration, ~$155 to ~$709 per housing. High-turn consumable pull-through — filters follow every dryer and re-order on a cycle.
German-engineered treatment — protects his service reputation; he's the one who eats the callback when a cheap drop-shipped dryer fails.
The program, not just the product: KSI feeds qualified leads + co-markets in his Midwest corridor and supports honest lead times — the direct answer to his backorder scar.
